correctness.rationale: Connected domination in the line graph is equivalent to connectivity of the bipartite edge set and complete support on at least one bipartition shore. Deleting cycle edges and nonspanning-shore leaves yields necessary bipartite-tree conditions; the converse checks every edge deletion, with a separate proof that one-deletion minimality implies inclusion-minimality. Bipartite Prüfer codes and surjections count each allowed tree exactly once. The theorem and endpoint counts include the m=n=2 boundary. An independent adjacency-based checker examined 1,444,991 nonempty vertex subsets over 17 graph orders and checked surjective words directly.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General exponential-time enumeration bounds produce a way to compute finite examples but not a uniform closed expression, gap theorem, or endpoint multiplicity for all rectangle dimensions; the statements do not imply those conclusions without the new structural and counting argument.

value.rationale: The coefficient formula fully classifies a natural nonmonotone minimality property on a two-parameter graph family, determines endpoint multiplicities and the upper connected domination number, and exposes a forbidden interval of cardinalities exactly for skew rectangles. This is not a mere reformulation of the known minimum connected domination number or a finite table computation.
